repo.description:
### Summary

A potential vulnerability exists in Zitadel's passkey registration endpoints. This endpoint allows registering a new passkey using a previously retrieved code. An improper expiration check of the code, could allow an attacker to potentially register their own passkey and gain access to the victim's account.

### Impact

Zitadel provides multiple way to register an additional passkey for an existing account. Among of them is the possibility to generate a code. This code is then typically sent to the authenticated user's email, which allows them to register a new device using the provided code within a predefined duration window.

Due to a improper handling of the validation of the code, failed attempts would reset the expiration window. An attacker could use this to their advantage to be able to reset an expired code.
This potentially allows the attacker to register their own device to the victim’s account, enabling a full account take over.
Note that an attacker would either need knowledge of an expired code or enumerate them. And while the expiration validation was faulty, multiple failed verifications would still permanently invalidate the code.

### Affected Versions

Systems running one of the following versions are affected:
- **4.x**: `4.0.0` through `4.12.1` (including RC versions)
- **3.x**: `3.0.0` through `3.4.7` (including RC versions)
- **2.x**: `2.0.0` through `2.71.19`

### Patches

The vulnerability has been addressed in the latest releases. The patch resolves the issue by correctly evaluating the expiration window.

- **4.x**: Upgrade to >=[4.12.2](https://github.com/zitadel/zitadel/releases/tag/v4.12.2)
- **3.x**: Update to >=[3.4.8](https://github.com/zitadel/zitadel/releases/tag/v3.4.8)
- **2.x**: Update to >=[3.4.8](https://github.com/zitadel/zitadel/releases/tag/v3.4.8)

### Workarounds

The recommended solution is to upgrade to a patched version.

### Questions

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please email us at [security@zitadel.com](mailto:security@zitadel.com)

### Credits

Thanks to [odgrso](https://github.com/odgrso) for reporting this vulnerability.
